chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: My master Anas narrated to us, he said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) went out to his companions and said: 'Whoever guarantees for me two [things], I will guarantee for him Paradise.' Abu Hurayrah said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I will guarantee them for you, what are they?' He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I will guarantee for him Paradise' — meaning, whoever guarantees for me his tongue and his private part — 'and the causes of calamities open from these two limbs, and the crime of the tongue is disbelief in Allah, speaking falsehood, slander, extravagance in the names and attributes of Allah, backbiting, gossip, and accusation, and that is from the crimes of the tongue; and the crime of the private part is intercourse where it is not permissible by marriage or ownership of the right hand.' Allah, the Exalted, said: 'And those who guard their private parts. Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two things the Prophet asked his companions to guarantee to ensure Paradise?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies the tongue and private part as the primary sources of human affliction, linking their restraint directly to Paradise. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue) against major sins like backbiting and disbelief, alongside *hifz al-farj* (guarding the private part) from unlawful sexual acts, reflecting a holistic approach to moral character.

en.basel-kadem: 98.	We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ahmad al-Tabari, that he said: We were told by Abu Sa’eed, that he said: We were told by Khirash, that he said: We were told by my master, Anas, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The one who says: «Glory be to Allah, and in the praise of Him» Allah will prescribe to him a thousand by a thousand good deed, erase from (the record of) him a thousand by a thousand misdeed and raise him by a thousand by a thousand degree. Moreover, the one who increases, Allah will increase to him, and the one who asks forgiveness, Allah will forgive him.
